paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is the Rock, and a Rock doesn't move. Moses sings that His work is perfect, that "all His ways are just," and that He is "a God of faithfulness without injustice" (Deuteronomy 32:4). Everything else in this song hangs off that one line. When people drift, the Rock is still sitting right where He always was.

And the song shows us how the drifting happens. God found His people in a howling wilderness, carried them like an eagle, and fed them honey from a rock (Deuteronomy 32:10-13). Then Jeshurun "grew fat and kicked" and "abandoned the God who made him" (Deuteronomy 32:15). I think that's the warning for us, baker. The danger isn't always the hard season. Sometimes it's the full-belly season, when we stop remembering who filled it.

But the song doesn't end in the dark. God says there is no God besides Him, and that no one can deliver from His hand (Deuteronomy 32:39). He will have compassion on His servants when He sees their strength is gone (Deuteronomy 32:36), and that means you can come back to Him with empty hands. So remember where your bread came from, thank the Rock out loud, and keep the apron on, because this story isn't over yet.
